The learned counsel for the appellants pointed out the pleadings, evidence, grounds of objection in the appeal and cross- objections, and also the reasons and findings.
It is submitted that the claimants' land were acquired for Submergence of Kolsur Medium Project.
The State Government has preferred the appeals, and the claimants have preferred the cross-objections.
It is further submitted that the evidence was not properly appreciated.
The Reference Court did not consider the sale exemplar of 1998 of the same village, by which 01 H 05 R land was sold for  4,50,000/-.
It is lastly prayed that the cross-objections be allowed and the appeals be dismissed.
3. The learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the acquired lands of the claimants had the facility of water through a well.
He further submitted that the valuation report and the e- statement corroborate the said contentions.
It is, therefore, prayed that compensation be awarded at double the rate of the sale exemplar i.e. Exhibit 34, wherein the land is admittedly shown as seasonally irrigated and not semi irrigated.
4. The learned AGP for the appellants submitted the sale instance was rightly considered.

It is further submitted that the Shrikant Malani Page 2 of 5  920.FA.1392.2010 compensation claimed and awarded by the learned Reference Court is Jayant Ashokrao More vs The State Of Mah And Ors on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95674825/

sentences.text: The learned AGP, therefore, prayed that the appeals be allowed by setting aside the impugned judgment and award.
5. The record and proceedings, as well as the grounds of objection in the appeals and cross-objections have been perused.
It is an admitted position that the sale exemplar of the year 1998 was executed for a consideration of  4,50,000/-, whereby, land admeasuring 01 H 05 R was sold.

6. In paragraph No.6 of the said impugned judgment, the learned Reference Court declined to accept the said sale exemplar of the year 1998, though it appears to be a bona fide and comparable sale instance.
There appears to be no justifiable reason to discard the sale exemplar.

If the said sale exemplar is taken into consideration, the claimants would be entitled to compensation at the same rate i.e.
2,141/- per Are for the acquired land.
7. If 1/4th of the amount is deducted from Rs.2,141/- the remaining amount comes to  1,606/- per Are, which can be taken as the value of non irrigated land.
The claimants' land is fully irrigated
As regards the valuation, the same has not been challenged by the claimants.

Therefore, this Court finds no substance in the grounds of objection raised in the appeals filed by the State, and the Jayant Ashokrao More vs The State Of Mah And Ors on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95674825/

The cross-objections filed by the claimants deserve to be partly allowed.
Hence, the following order.
ORDER  A) The appeals are dismissed.
B) The cross-objections are allowed.
C) The impugned judgment and award is partly set  aside and modified as under :
D) The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.3,212/- per R, which includes earlier amount paid to the claimants along with accrued interest and costs etc.

E) The claimants are also entitled for statutory benefits like additional components,
interest and solatium as per the provisions of Land Acquisition Act.
F) The claimants are not entitled for statutory benefits 920.FA.1392.2010 i.e. solatium, interest and components etc for the delayed period.
G) The State Government is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation in this Court within a period of 12 weeks from today along with accrued interest, if any.
H) The claimants shall deposit the amount of deficit Court Fees, if any.
I) The Registry is directed to disburse the said amount in the bank accounts of the claimants.
J) The record and proceedings be sent back.

( SANJAY A. DESHMUKH, J. )
